title: Facebook launches Creator Studio AI app for creators
excerpt: Creator Studio promises to help Facebook creators understand their audiences without getting lost in analytics.
content_html:
Creator Studio promises to help Facebook creators understand their audiences without getting lost in analytics.

 

By

Olivia Tauber

Olivia Tauber

Deputy Digital Culture Editor

Olivia Tauber is the deputy editor of digital culture, covering creators, media, movies, beauty, and more. Based in New York, her work has appeared in The New York Times, Vanity Fair, The Cut, Teen Vogue, Complex, and Interview Magazine. She holds a Master's degree in Journalism from NYU and a Bachelor's from the University of Michigan. She also runs Fan Mail, a weekly pop-culture newsletter.

Facebook wants to help creators spend less time deciphering analytics and more time making content. Its solution is, naturally, another app.

On Aug. 12, the company officially rolled out its revamped Creator Studio, a stand-alone app that uses AI to help creators understand their performance, plan their next posts, and respond to followers. The launch follows a limited test that began in June.

Meta describes the new iPhone app as an "AI-powered daily companion for Facebook creators." Its pitch boils down to three tasks: mapping out a creator’s daily priorities, offering personalized tips to grow, and helping them reply to fans with AI.

You May Also Like

The app is now available on iOS to Facebook creators in the United States and Canada. An Android version is expected later.

What can creators expect from Creator Studio?

Creator Studio is designed as an integrated workspace for people who manage their accounts through Facebook but inevitably get pulled into Reels, messages, and the feed. When creators open the app, they see a list of daily priorities, which might include reviewing a recent post, checking progress toward a goal, or responding to comments.

Mashable Trend Report

At the center of the app is Facebook’s AI creator assistant, which the company first introduced in June. The assistant draws from a creator’s content, performance, audience engagement, and stated goals to offer personalized recommendations.

Instead of digging through analytics dashboards, creators can ask questions like, “When should I post?” or “Why did this Reel perform better than my others?” They can then ask follow-up questions about changes in their audience or ways to improve their next post. The assistant can also suggest formats, trends, and other creators in a similar niche to learn from.

Creator Studio can also help manage the comments section. The app identifies comments that may be worth answering, and drafts replies in what Facebook says is the creator's usual tone. Creators can edit or approve each response before it is published.

Facebook says some early testers have already changed their content strategies based on the app’s recommendations. Food and wellness creator Mymanabites told Facebook that she tried a format suggested through Creator Studio and gained 4,000 followers from one video, with 82 percent of its audience coming from non-followers. Content creator and filmmaker Michael Tushouse said the assistant helped increase his earnings by 144 percent during his first seven days using the strategy.

The pitch is convenient for creators, but it’s also strategic for Meta. TikTok’s AI Outline transforms a prompt or trending search topic into a video title, hook, hashtags, and outline. YouTube’s Ask Studio summarizes comments, explains channel performance, and brainstorms video ideas, while its Inspiration tab suggests topics based on what audiences are watching. Creator Studio brings Facebook versions of these same tools as platforms compete to become the hub where creators plan content, publish it, and grow their businesses.

Creator Studio also joins Meta’s recent parade of stand-alone apps. This year, the company released Forum, a Reddit-like home for Facebook Groups, and tested Instants, an app for sending disappearing photos to Instagram friends. Meta also released Seller, an iPhone app for managing Facebook Marketplace listings and buyer messages, and began testing StoryKit, an AI app that creates personalized children’s stories, in select markets.

The app’s success will depend on whether creators find its advice useful enough to incorporate into their routines. If Meta gets its way, Creator Studio will become the app creators open before they open Facebook.

8 月 12 日，该公司正式推出了改版后的 Creator Studio，这是一款独立的应用程序，它使用 AI 来帮助创作者了解他们的表现、计划他们的下一篇文章并回复关注者。 此次发布是在六月份开始的有限测试之后进行的。

Meta 将这款新 iPhone 应用描述为“Facebook 创作者的人工智能日常伴侣”。 它的宣传可以归结为三项任务：制定创作者的日常优先事项、提供个性化的成长技巧以及帮助他们利用人工智能回复粉丝。

创作者对创作者工作室有何期望？

Creator Studio 被设计为一个集成工作空间，供那些通过 Facebook 管理帐户但又不可避免地陷入 Reels、消息和 feed 的人们使用。 当创作者打开应用程序时，他们会看到每日优先事项列表，其中可能包括查看最近的帖子、检查目标进度或回复评论。

可混搭趋势报告

该应用程序的核心是 Facebook 的人工智能创作者助手，该公司于 6 月份首次推出。 助手根据创作者的内容、表演、观众参与度和既定目标来提供个性化推荐。

创建者可以提出诸如“我应该什么时候发布？”之类的问题，而不是深入分析分析仪表板。 或“为什么这个卷轴比我的其他卷轴表现更好？” 然后，他们可以提出有关受众变化或改进下一篇文章的方法的后续问题。 助手还可以建议类似领域的格式、趋势和其他创作者以供学习。

Creator Studio 还可以帮助管理评论部分。 该应用程序会识别可能值得回复的评论，并以 Facebook 所说的创作者惯常的语气起草回复。 创建者可以在发布之前编辑或批准每个回复。

Facebook 表示，一些早期测试人员已经根据应用程序的建议改变了他们的内容策略。 食品和健康创作者 Mymanabites 告诉 Facebook，她尝试了 Creator Studio 建议的格式，并从一个视频中获得了 4,000 名粉丝，其中 82% 的观众来自非粉丝。 内容创作者兼电影制片人迈克尔·图斯豪斯 (Michael Tushouse) 表示，在他使用该策略的头 7 天内，助手帮助他的收入增加了 144%。

推介对创作者来说很方便，但对 Meta 来说也具有战略意义。 TikTok 的 AI Outline 将提示或趋势搜索主题转换为视频标题、挂钩、主题标签和大纲。 YouTube 的 Ask Studio 总结评论、解释频道表现并集思广益视频创意，而其“灵感”选项卡则根据观众正在观看的内容建议主题。 随着平台竞相成为创作者规划内容、发布内容和发展业务的中心，Creator Studio 也带来了这些相同工具的 Facebook 版本。

Creator Studio 也加入了 Meta 最近的独立应用程序行列。 今年，该公司发布了 Forum（一个类似于 Reddit 的 Facebook Groups 主页），并测试了 Instants（一款用于向 Instagram 好友发送消失照片的应用程序）。 Meta 还发布了 Seller（一款用于管理 Facebook Marketplace 列表和买家消息的 iPhone 应用程序），并开始在特定市场测试 StoryKit（一款创建个性化儿童故事的 AI 应用程序）。

该应用程序的成功将取决于创作者是否认为其建议足够有用，可以将其融入到他们的日常生活中。 如果 Meta 成功的话，Creator Studio 将成为应用程序创建者在打开 Facebook 之前打开的应用程序。

数字文化副编辑

Olivia Tauber 是《数字文化》副主编，内容涵盖创作者、媒体、电影、美妆等。 她居住在纽约，作品曾出现在《纽约时报》、《名利场》、《The Cut》、《Teen Vogue》、《Complex》和《Interview》杂志上。 她拥有纽约大学新闻学硕士学位和密歇根大学学士学位。 她还经营《粉丝邮报》（Fan Mail），这是一份每周流行文化时事通讯。
